steps.title: Why this paper
steps.explanation: In 2017 a team at Google removed recurrence entirely — and almost every model you have used since is built on what replaced it.

steps.title: The title
steps.explanation: It is called Attention Is All You Need — and the title is the entire claim.

steps.title: The route
steps.explanation: We will do this in four moves: the problem attention solved, the idea itself, the machine it builds, and the proof that it worked.

steps.title: The promise
steps.explanation: By the end you will be able to read the architecture diagram like a map of one idea applied three ways.

steps.title: The old world
steps.explanation: Before 2017, a model read a sentence the way you read this one: one word at a time, in order.

steps.title: The wait
steps.explanation: Word four cannot start until word three is finished — so the whole sentence costs the sum of its words.

steps.title: The price
steps.explanation: Order was paid for with time, and time was the one thing training could not buy more of.

scenes.title: Idea
scenes.director: This is the thesis, so we spend the scene's one hero moment: you full frame, the room dims behind you, and one line glows at your side — keep attention, drop everything else. Nothing else moves. Then the page strikes out recurrence under the claim, and the video never looks back.

steps.title: The claim
steps.explanation: Keep attention — the mechanism that lets every word look at every other word — and drop everything else.

steps.title: The deletion
steps.explanation: No recurrence, no convolution. The network keeps only the part that was never the bottleneck.

steps.title: The whole machine
steps.explanation: Here is the entire transformer: an encoder on the left, a decoder on the right, and a bridge of attention between them.

steps.title: Six identical layers
steps.explanation: Each side is the same layer stamped six times — tokens flow in at the bottom, meaning flows out at the top.

steps.title: The residual path
steps.explanation: Every layer adds its answer to the input instead of replacing it — that bypass is what lets six layers behave like one idea.

scenes.title: Scaled dot product
scenes.director: Half a sentence on you, then straight into the mechanism — the flow diagram takes the frame, chip small. Walk the arrows: queries meet keys, divide by the square root, softmax, weigh the values. The multiplication is the hero of the scene: let it pulse before you say the word “scaled”.

steps.title: The atom
steps.explanation: Everything in the paper is one operation repeated: scaled dot-product attention.

steps.title: Queries meet keys
steps.explanation: Each word asks a question — its query — and every word answers with a key; the match score is just a dot product.

steps.title: Scaled and weighed
steps.explanation: Divide by the square root of the key size so the scores stay sane, softmax them into weights, and take the weighted sum of the values.

steps.title: One is not enough
steps.explanation: A single attention pattern can only look for one kind of relationship at a time.

steps.title: Eight views at once
steps.explanation: So the model runs eight in parallel — one head tracks grammar, one tracks distance, the rest find patterns nobody named.

steps.title: The merge
steps.explanation: The eight views are concatenated and projected back into one stream — many eyes, one voice.

scenes.title: Three uses
scenes.director: Same block, three jobs — keep yourself in a panel and the page beside you; this is orientation, not machinery. Point at each use as you name it: encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention, then the cross-attention bridge. The bridge earns the scene's one hand-over — it is the one people misread.

steps.title: Three places
steps.explanation: The same attention block appears in exactly three places, and each placement means something different.

steps.title: Self attention, twice
steps.explanation: In the encoder every word reads every word; in the decoder each word may only read the past.

steps.title: The bridge
steps.explanation: Cross-attention is the third use: the decoder's questions are answered by the encoder's memory — this is the one to watch.

steps.title: The missing sense
steps.explanation: Attention alone cannot tell first from fifth — the set of words is right, the order is gone.

steps.title: A fingerprint per position
steps.explanation: So each position adds its own signature of sine waves — order injected without a single recurrent step.

steps.title: Three costs
steps.explanation: The paper scores every layer type on three costs: compute per layer, sequential work, and path length between distant words.

steps.title: The winning row
steps.explanation: Self-attention is constant in the two columns that matter — any two words are one hop apart.

steps.title: The argument
steps.explanation: That O(1) is the whole argument: long-range dependencies stop being expensive.

steps.title: The scores
steps.explanation: On both WMT 2014 translation tasks the transformer set the state of the art — 28.4 and 41.8 BLEU.

steps.title: The price
steps.explanation: And it did it for a fraction of the training cost of the models it beat.

steps.title: The claim
steps.explanation: Better results for less compute — that is why the field moved in a year.
